title: Al Hayes, baritone chairs and becoming straw boss
summary: Cobb recalls Al Hayes and the sax section shuffle when Rudy Rutherford and Jack McVea left or fell sick, how he became straw boss and got a four-dollar raise per night.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Now, you mentioned Fred Beckett and Al Hayes. Well, Fred Beckett, people know about him, you know, as a very good trumpet player and (inaudible) band, you know --
He was a very good trombone player.

I don't know. I really couldn't tell you, but I know he's still alive, and from Henry Mills (inaudible) I told you the drummer that played with me (inaudible) in the postal service, still is in Detroit, said Al was doing fine (inaudible) before I got on it.
And, you know, naturally I'm quite interested in guys that have been my close friends. Yet we don't keep in close touch. I like to know how they're doing, you know.
He was playing baritone when I got in the band.
And when Rudy Rutherford, who's with Earl Hines now, left --

-- and then he got over on the alto side, and I played baritone and tenor in the band, coming back down until Rudy come back to the band and Jack got back on the baritone. Then eventually when Jack took sick, Rudy had to play baritone, and he took sick in Wheeling, West Virginia, and the doctor told him he couldn't blow for a while, about a couple of three months, and -- and that's how I took over the straw boss situation of the band. Jack had it.

So Hamp let Stan -- and Jack was sick, I was taking over anyway for -- and when he come back (inaudible) Jack back home to California, he told me to keep it, and he gave me a raise (inaudible) per night, that is, per night, per night, $4.00 of raise per night on my salary.
